antwerpen-be.name: Antwerpen
antwerpen-be.general: Antwerp is a city and a municipality in the Flemish Region of Belgium. It is the capital and largest city of Antwerp Province, and the third-largest municipality in Belgium by area at 208.22 km2 (80.39 sq mi). With a population of 565,039, it is the most populous municipality in Belgium, and with a metropolitan population of over 1.2 million people, the country's second-largest metropolitan area after Brussels.

brussels-be.name: Brussels
brussels-be.general: The City of Brussels is the largest municipality and historical centre of the Brussels-Capital Region, as well as the capital of Belgium. It is additionally the capital of the French Community of Belgium, the Flemish Community, and the Flemish Region. The City of Brussels is also the administrative centre of the European Union, as it hosts a number of principal EU institutions in its European Quarter.
brussels-be.tagline: municipality in the Brussels-Capital Region and capital of Belgium.
activities: Visit a flagship botanical garden or city park late afternoon
Take a tram or metro across the city purely for the architecture
Eat where the locals queue at lunchtime, not where the tourists sit
Climb to a viewpoint above the centre for the panorama
tips: Reserved-seat trains are sometimes much cheaper booked two weeks ahead.
Sunday closures hit shops and offices, not restaurants.
Museum slots sell out on weekends in Brussels

zagreb-hr.name: Zagreb
zagreb-hr.general: Zagreb is the capital and largest city of Croatia. It is in the north of the country, along the Sava River, at the southern slopes of the Medvednica mountain. Zagreb stands near the international border between Croatia and Slovenia at an elevation of approximately 158 m (518 ft) above sea level.
zagreb-hr.tagline: Capital city and county in Croatia.
activities: Pick one flagship museum and skip the second
Drive a short loop into the surrounding peaks for the view
Eat a regional alpine dish at a mountain-style inn
Walk the historic core's main square circuit
tips: Weather can shift fast in mountain capitals — check the forecast hour by hour.
Funiculars and trams are often a faster shortcut than walking uphill.
Coastal parking fills fast in summer — arrive early

nicosia-cy.name: Nicosia
nicosia-cy.general: Nicosia, also known as Lefkosia or Lefkoşa, is the capital of Cyprus. It is the southeasternmost capital city among European Union member states. Its northern part is the de facto capital of Northern Cyprus.
nicosia-cy.tagline: Capital of the Republic of Cyprus.
activities: Drive (or bus) to a panoramic viewpoint outside the city
Eat at a backstreet taverna away from the cruise route
Take a half-day ferry to a smaller neighbouring island
Walk the historic core in a single morning loop
tips: Rental scooters are everywhere — wear a helmet, locals do.
Island taxis are scarce; pre-book one if you have an early flight.
Morning light is best for photos and walks

brno-cz.name: Brno
brno-cz.general: Brno is a city in the South Moravian Region of the Czech Republic. Located at the confluence of the Svitava and Svratka rivers, Brno has about 404,000 inhabitants, making it the second-largest city in the Czech Republic after the capital, Prague, and one of the 100 largest cities in the European Union. The Brno metropolitan area has approximately 730,000 inhabitants.
brno-cz.tagline: Statutory city in the Czech Republic.
activities: Visit a museum of mountaineering or alpine culture
Walk a circuit of the old town and main cathedral
Drive a half-hour into the peaks for a panoramic viewpoint
Take the funicular or cable car to the city's overlook
tips: Cable cars often close in high wind — confirm before buying tickets.
Pack walking shoes for cobbles and a layer for evenings even in July.
Card payments are widely accepted in cities

prague-cz.name: Prague
prague-cz.general: Prague is the capital and largest city of the Czech Republic and the historical capital of Bohemia. Located on the Vltava River, the city has a population of about 1.4 million, making it the twelfth-largest city in the European Union. Its metropolitan area is home to approximately 2.3 million people.
prague-cz.tagline: Capital and largest city of the Czech Republic.
activities: Catch a free organ recital at the main cathedral if scheduled
Climb to a viewpoint above the centre for the panorama
Take a tram or metro across the city purely for the architecture
Eat where the locals queue at lunchtime, not where the tourists sit
tips: Reserved-seat trains are sometimes much cheaper booked two weeks ahead.
Sunday closures hit shops and offices, not restaurants.
Prague crowds peak late morning — start sights early

copenhagen-dk.name: Copenhagen
copenhagen-dk.general: Copenhagen is the capital and most populous city of Denmark, with an urban population of 1.4 million. The city is situated mainly on the island of Zealand (Sjælland), with a smaller part on the island of Amager. Copenhagen is separated from Malmö, Sweden, by the Øresund strait.
copenhagen-dk.tagline: Capital and most populous city of Denmark.
activities: Tour a flagship maritime or naval museum
Browse a market street where the catch is unloaded each morning
Try the city's signature seafood dish at a local konoba/taverna
Walk the historic waterfront at golden hour
tips: Cruise-ship days swamp the old town between 09:00 and 16:00; aim for early or late.
Tap water is fine in most coastal capitals — refill a bottle to save money.
Bikes have priority — check bike lanes before turning

tallinn-ee.general: Tallinn is the capital and largest city of Estonia. As of 2024, the population of the Tallinn metropolitan area is estimated at 646,315. Tallinn is the main governmental, financial, industrial, and cultural centre of Estonia. It is located 187 kilometres (116 mi) northwest of the country's second largest city, Tartu, however, only 80 kilometres (50 mi) south of Helsinki, Finland.
tallinn-ee.tagline: Capital and largest city of Estonia.
activities: Climb the city's highest viewpoint for a panoramic sweep

Tour a flagship maritime or naval museum
Walk the historic waterfront at golden hour
tips: Cruise-ship days swamp the old town between 09:00 and 16:00; aim for early or late.
Ferries to popular islands sell out fast in summer — book ahead.
Sauna culture is common — bring a towel

espoo-fi.name: Espoo
espoo-fi.general: Espoo is a city in Finland. It is located to the west of the capital, Helsinki, in southern Uusimaa. The population is approximately 326,000. It is the 2nd most populous municipality in Finland. Espoo is part of the Helsinki Metropolitan Area, which has approximately 1.6 million inhabitants. The city includes the enclave of Kauniainen. Espoo covers an area of 528 km2 (204 sq mi).

helsinki-fi.name: Helsinki

activities: Visit the cathedral and the city's flagship museum

Walk a circuit of the centro storico and main square
tips: Regional train tickets sometimes need stamping or scanning before boarding.
Lunch menus are often half the price of evening menus for the same dish.
Bread and café culture reward slow mornings

activities: Try the regional dish at a back-street trattoria
Walk a circuit of the centro storico and main square

marseille-fr.name: Marseille
marseille-fr.general: Marseille is a city in southern France, the prefecture of the Bouches-du-Rhône department and of the Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur region. Situated in Provence, it marks the eastern end of the Côte Bleue on the Mediterranean coast. Marseille is the second-most populous city proper in France, after Paris, with 886,040 inhabitants in 2023 over a municipal territory of 241 km2 (93 sq mi).
activities: Sample the regional seafood at a quayside taverna
Take a half-day boat tour to a nearby cove
Stroll the seafront and old harbour at dusk
Climb to the citadel or ramparts above the bay
tips: The first ferry of the morning is the quietest if you're island-hopping.
Many beaches charge for loungers; public stretches are free if you bring a towel.
Many museums close one weekday — check ahead

nantes-fr.general: Nantes is a city in the Loire-Atlantique department of France on the Loire, 50 km (31 mi) from the Atlantic coast. The city is the sixth largest in France, with a population of 327,734 in Nantes proper (2023) and a metropolitan area of 1,050,815 inhabitants (2023). With Saint-Nazaire, a seaport on the Loire estuary, Nantes forms one of the main north-western French metropolitan agglomerations.

toulouse-fr.name: Toulouse
toulouse-fr.general: Toulouse is a city in Southern France, the prefecture of the Haute-Garonne department and of the Occitania region. The city is on the banks of the River Garonne, 150 kilometres from the Mediterranean Sea, 230 km (143 mi) from the Atlantic Ocean and 680 km (420 mi) from Paris.
activities: Climb the bell tower or castle for the rooftops view
Browse the weekly market for produce and crafts
Try the regional dish at a back-street trattoria
Visit the cathedral and the city's flagship museum
tips: Lunch menus are often half the price of evening menus for the same dish.
Cash still appears at smaller bakeries and family restaurants.
Bread and café culture reward slow mornings

hamburg-de.name: Hamburg
hamburg-de.general: Hamburg, officially the Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg, is the second-largest city in Germany after Berlin and sixth-largest city in the European Union, with a population of over 1.9 million. The Hamburg Metropolitan Region has a population of over 5.1 million and is the tenth-largest metropolitan region by GDP in the European Union.
activities: Take a half-day boat trip along the coast
Spend a sunset at a rooftop bar with a sea view
Hop on a coastal tram or harbour ferry for the architecture
Eat at a fish market where chefs queue for the day's catch
tips: Late August empties some quarters but fills the parks — plan accordingly.
Pick a single neighbourhood rather than trying to see everything.
Pfand applies on bottles — return at supermarkets

hamburg-mitte-de.name: Hamburg-Mitte
hamburg-mitte-de.general: Hamburg-Mitte is one of the seven boroughs of Hamburg, Germany, covering most of the city's urban center. The quarters of Hamburg-Altstadt and Neustadt cover much of the city's historic core. In 2020 the population was 301,231.
activities: Walk a coastal path out of town for the panoramic view back
Take a half-day boat tour to a nearby cove
Stroll the seafront and old harbour at dusk
tips: Many beaches charge for loungers; public stretches are free if you bring a towel.
Coastal cities heat up after 11:00 in summer — start sights early.
Pfand applies on bottles — return at supermarkets

hamburg-nord-de.name: Hamburg-Nord
hamburg-nord-de.general: Hamburg-Nord is one of the seven boroughs of the Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg, in northern Germany. In 2020, according to the residents registration office, the population was 315,514 in an area of 57.5 km2.
activities: Walk a coastal path out of town for the panoramic view back
Stroll the seafront and old harbour at dusk
Take a half-day boat tour to a nearby cove
Visit the city's archaeological or maritime museum
tips: Coastal cities heat up after 11:00 in summer — start sights early.
Many beaches charge for loungers; public stretches are free if you bring a towel.
Cash still appears in smaller bakeries

The Hanover Region has some 1.16 million inhabitants (2019) and is the largest in the Hanover–Braunschweig–Göttingen–Wolfsburg Metropolitan Region, the 17th biggest metropolitan area by GDP in the European Union.

munich-de.general: Munich is the capital and most populous city of Bavaria, Germany. Munich is the largest city in Germany that is not a state of its own, and it ranks as the 11th-largest city in the European Union (EU). The metropolitan area has around 3 million inhabitants, and the broader Munich Metropolitan Region is home to about 6.2 million people. It is the seat of the Upper Bavarian administrative region.

munster-de.general: Münster is an independent city in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It is in the northern part of the state and the historic capital of the Westphalia region, as well being the centre of a state district. During the Protestant Reformation, Münster was the location of the Anabaptist rebellion. Münster and Osnabrück were the sites of the signing of the Treaties of Westphalia which ended the Thirty Years' War in 1648.

stuttgart-de.name: Stuttgart
stuttgart-de.general: Stuttgart is the capital and largest city of the German state of Baden-Württemberg. It is located on the Neckar river in a fertile valley known as the Stuttgarter Kessel and lies an hour from the Swabian Jura and the Black Forest.
activities: Browse the weekly market for produce and crafts
Catch sunset from a riverside or hillside vantage point
Try the regional dish at a back-street trattoria
Walk a circuit of the centro storico and main square
tips: Cash still appears at smaller bakeries and family restaurants.
Most museums shut one weekday — usually Monday or Tuesday.
Regional train tickets sometimes need validation

wandsbek-de.name: Wandsbek
wandsbek-de.general: Wandsbek is the second-largest of seven boroughs that make up the city and state of Hamburg, Germany. The name of the district is derived from the river Wandse which passes through here. Wandsbek, which was formerly an independent city, is urban and, along with Eilbek and Marienthal, part of the city's economic and cultural core. In 2020 the population was 442,702, making it the most populous borough in Hamburg.

Take a half-day boat tour to a nearby cove

wuppertal-de.name: Wuppertal
wuppertal-de.general: Wuppertal is a city in North Rhine-Westphalia, in western Germany, with a population of 355,000. Wuppertal is the seventh-largest city in North Rhine-Westphalia and 17th-largest in Germany. It was founded in 1929 by the merger of Elberfeld, Barmen, Ronsdorf, Cronenberg and Vohwinkel, and was initially called "Barmen-Elberfeld" before adopting its present name in 1930.
activities: Catch sunset from a riverside or hillside vantage point

Try the regional dish at a back-street trattoria
Browse the weekly market for produce and crafts
tips: Most museums shut one weekday — usually Monday or Tuesday.
Cash still appears at smaller bakeries and family restaurants.
Sunday shopping is limited outside train stations

athens-gr.name: Athens
athens-gr.general: Athens is the capital and largest city of Greece. A significant coastal urban area in the Mediterranean, Athens is also the capital of the Attica region and is the southernmost capital on the European mainland. With its urban area's population numbering over 3.6 million, it is the eighth-largest urban area in the European Union (EU).
athens-gr.tagline: capital and largest city of Greece.

Walk the historic waterfront at golden hour
Take a ferry or harbour cruise across the bay
Ride a tram or vaporetto across the historic centre

buda-hu.name: Buda
buda-hu.general: Buda is the part of Budapest, the capital city of Hungary, that lies on the western bank of the Danube. Historically, "Buda" referred only to the royal walled city on Castle Hill, which was constructed by Béla IV between 1247 and 1249 and subsequently served as the capital of the Kingdom of Hungary from 1361 to 1873. In 1873, Buda was administratively unified with Pest and Óbuda to form modern Budapest.
buda-hu.tagline: Ancient capital of the Kingdom of Hungary.
activities: Sample a regional alpine or highland dish
Drive a half-hour into the peaks for a panoramic viewpoint
Visit a museum of mountaineering or alpine culture
Take the funicular or cable car to the city's overlook
tips: Daylight is shorter inside valleys than on open coast — plan sunset early.
Pack walking shoes for cobbles and a layer for evenings even in July.
Danube views are best at golden hour

budapest-hu.name: Budapest

It is Hungary's primate city with 1.7 million inhabitants and its greater metro area has a population of about 3.3 million, representing one-third of the country's population and producing more than 40% of the country's economic output.
budapest-hu.tagline: Capital and largest city of Hungary.
activities: Drive a short loop into the surrounding peaks for the view
Pick one flagship museum and skip the second
Eat a regional alpine dish at a mountain-style inn
Take the city's funicular or cable car for the panorama
tips: Weather can shift fast in mountain capitals — check the forecast hour by hour.
Altitude changes inside the city — pack a layer even in summer.
Danube views are best at golden hour

pest-hu.name: Pest
pest-hu.general: Pest is the part of Budapest, the capital city of Hungary, that lies on the eastern bank of the Danube. Pest was administratively unified with Buda and Óbuda in 1873. Prior to this, it was an independent city.
activities: Spend a morning in one historic neighbourhood, not the whole city
Eat at a market hall surrounded by produce stalls
Take a regional train one hour out for a contrasting day trip
See live music in a neighbourhood venue, not a tourist hall
tips: Pick a single neighbourhood rather than trying to see everything.
Late August empties some quarters but fills the parks — plan accordingly.
Thermal baths need flip-flops and sometimes caps

reykjavik-is.name: Reykjavik
reykjavik-is.general: Reykjavík is the capital and largest city of Iceland. It is located on the southern shore of the Faxaflói bay in southwest Iceland and has a latitude of 64°08′ N, making it the world's northernmost capital of a sovereign state. Reykjavík has a population of around 140,000 as of 2026, and the surrounding Capital Region has a population of around 252,000, constituting approximately 64% of Iceland's population.
reykjavik-is.tagline: Capital and most populous city of Iceland.
activities: Walk the historic waterfront at golden hour
Take a ferry or harbour cruise across the bay
Visit the old port and the lighthouse at dusk
Try the city's signature seafood dish at a local konoba/taverna
tips: Ferries to popular islands sell out fast in summer — book ahead.
Old-town stone is slick after rain — pack grippy shoes.
Fuel stops are sparse outside Ring Road towns

bologna-it.name: Bologna
bologna-it.general: Bologna is the capital and largest city of the Emilia-Romagna region in northern Italy. It is the seventh most populous city in Italy, with 391,473 inhabitants from 150 different nationalities. Its metropolitan province is home to more than 1 million people as of 2026. Bologna is most famous for being the home to the oldest university in continuous operation, the University of Bologna, established in AD 1088.
bologna-it.tagline: Capital and largest city of Emilia-Romagna, Italy.
activities: Take the funicular or cable car to the city's overlook
Sample a regional alpine or highland dish
Walk a riverside or canyon path on the edge of the city
Walk a circuit of the old town and main cathedral
tips: Pack walking shoes for cobbles and a layer for evenings even in July.
Daylight is shorter inside valleys than on open coast — plan sunset early.
Coperto and service charges appear on bills

catania-it.name: Catania
catania-it.general: Catania is the second-largest city in the autonomous island region of Sicily in Italy, after Palermo, both by area and by population. Despite being the second largest city of the island, Catania is the centre of the most densely populated Sicilian conurbation, which is among the largest in Italy. It has important road and rail transport infrastructures, and hosts the main airport of Sicily.
activities: Sample the regional seafood at a quayside taverna
Take a half-day boat tour to a nearby cove
Walk a coastal path out of town for the panoramic view back
Climb to the citadel or ramparts above the bay
tips: The first ferry of the morning is the quietest if you're island-hopping.
Many beaches charge for loungers; public stretches are free if you bring a towel.
ZTL zones in historic centres — check parking

The city's wider metropolitan area is the largest in Italy, and the fourth-largest in the European Union, with an estimated population of 6.55 million.

turin-it.name: Turin
turin-it.general: Turin is a city and a business and cultural centre in northern Italy. It is the capital city of the Piedmont region and of the Metropolitan City of Turin. From 1861 to 1865, it was the first capital of the Kingdom of Italy. The city is mainly on the western bank of the River Po, below its Susa Valley, and is surrounded by the western Alpine arch and Superga hill.
activities: Walk a riverside or canyon path on the edge of the city
Drive a half-hour into the peaks for a panoramic viewpoint
Walk a circuit of the old town and main cathedral
Visit a museum of mountaineering or alpine culture
tips: Cable cars often close in high wind — confirm before buying tickets.
Daylight is shorter inside valleys than on open coast — plan sunset early.
August closures in cities, crowds on coast

szczecin-pl.general: Szczecin, historically known in English as Stettin, is the capital and largest city of the West Pomeranian Voivodeship in northwestern Poland. Located near the Baltic Sea and the German border, it is a major seaport, the largest city of northwestern Poland, and seventh-largest city of Poland. As of 31 December 2022, the population was 391,566.

warsaw-pl.name: Warsaw
warsaw-pl.general: Warsaw, officially the Capital City of Warsaw, is the capital and most populous city of Poland. The metropolis stands on the river Vistula in east-central Poland. Its population is officially estimated at 1.87 million residents within a greater metropolitan area of around 3.5 million residents, which makes Warsaw the 7th most populous city in the European Union.
warsaw-pl.tagline: Capital and largest city of Poland.
activities: Take a tram or metro across the city purely for the architecture
Walk the historic core in a single morning loop

Catch a free organ recital at the main cathedral if scheduled
tips: Reserved-seat trains are sometimes much cheaper booked two weeks ahead.
Many flagship museums close one weekday — check before you go.
Salt mines and Auschwitz need timed tickets

wrocaw-pl.name: Wrocław

It lies on the banks of the Oder (Odra) River in the Silesian Lowlands. In 2025, the official population of Wrocław was 672,545, making it the third-largest city in Poland. The population of the Wrocław metropolitan area is around 1.25 million.

lisbon-pt.name: Lisbon
lisbon-pt.general: Lisbon is the capital and most populous city of Portugal, with an estimated population of 658,236 as of 2025, within its administrative limits and 3,353,000 within the metropolis, as of 2025. The city lies on the Atlantic Ocean in the western part of the Iberian Peninsula, fronting the northern shore of the River Tagus.
lisbon-pt.tagline: Capital and largest city of Portugal.
activities: Try the city's signature seafood dish at a local konoba/taverna

bucharest-ro.name: Bucharest
bucharest-ro.general: Bucharest is the capital and largest city of Romania. The metropolis stands on the River Dâmbovița in south-eastern Romania. Its population is officially estimated at 1.71 million residents within a greater metropolitan area of 2.31 million residents, which makes Bucharest the 9th most-populous city by population within city limits in the European Union.
bucharest-ro.tagline: Capital and largest city of Romania.

constanta-ro.name: Constanţa
constanta-ro.general: Constanța is a city in the Northern Dobruja historical region of Romania. Visit the city's archaeological or maritime museum

It lies on both banks of the Northern Dvina River, near its mouth into the White Sea. Arkhangelsk was the chief seaport of medieval and early modern Russia until 1703, when it was replaced by the newly founded Saint Petersburg.

belgrade-rs.name: Belgrade
belgrade-rs.general: Belgrade is the capital and historic largest city of Serbia. It is located at the confluence of the Sava and Danube rivers and at the crossroads of the Pannonian Plain and the Balkan Peninsula. According to the 2022 census, the population of Belgrade city proper stands at 1,197,114, its contiguous urban area has 1,298,661 inhabitants, while the population of the city's administrative area totals 1,682,720 people.
belgrade-rs.tagline: Capital and largest city of Serbia.

ljubljana-si.name: Ljubljana
ljubljana-si.general: Ljubljana is the capital and largest city of Slovenia, located along a trade route between the northern Adriatic Sea and the Danube region, north of the country's largest marsh, it has been inhabited since prehistoric times. It is the country's cultural, educational, economic, political and administrative centre and the seat of the Urban Municipality of Ljubljana.
ljubljana-si.tagline: Capital and largest city of Slovenia.

las-palmas-de-gran-canaria-es.general: Las Palmas, officially Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, is the capital and largest city of the autonomous community of the Canary Islands in Spain. With a population of 383,516 as of 2024, it is the ninth-largest city in Spain. It is also the fifth-most populous urban area in Spain and, depending on sources, ninth or tenth most populous metropolitan area in Spain.
activities: Try the regional dish at a back-street trattoria
Browse the weekly market for produce and crafts
Visit the cathedral and the city's flagship museum
Catch sunset from a riverside or hillside vantage point
tips: Cash still appears at smaller bakeries and family restaurants.
Regional train tickets sometimes need stamping or scanning before boarding.
Summer coast heat needs shade and water

murcia-es.name: Murcia
murcia-es.general: Murcia is a city in south-eastern Spain, and the capital and most populous city of the autonomous community of the Region of Murcia. As of 2024, with a population of 471,982, it is the 7th-largest city in Spain. The total population of the metropolitan area was 672,773 in 2020, covering an urban area of 1,230.9 km2. It is located on the Segura River, in the southeast of the Iberian Peninsula.
murcia-es.tagline: Municipality in Region of Murcia, Spain.
activities: Browse the weekly market for produce and crafts
Try the regional dish at a back-street trattoria
Walk a circuit of the centro storico and main square
Visit the cathedral and the city's flagship museum
tips: Cash still appears at smaller bakeries and family restaurants.
Most museums shut one weekday — usually Monday or Tuesday.
Summer coast heat needs shade and water

palma-es.name: Palma
palma-es.general: Palma is the capital of Spain. Palma or La Palma means palm in a number of languages and may also refer to: Topics referred to by the same term
palma-es.tagline: Topics referred to by the same term.
activities: Swim from a hidden cove signposted off the main road
Eat fresh seafood at a harbourside konoba
Walk the old town walls or kastro
Buy island wine, oil, or honey direct from a producer
tips: Cash is widely accepted but cards work in most central restaurants now.
Island weather can change quickly — bring a light layer even in summer.
Dinner starts late — restaurants open after 20:00

sevilla-es.general: Seville is the capital and largest city of the Spanish autonomous community of Andalusia and the province of Seville. It is situated on the lower reaches of the River Guadalquivir, in the southwest of the Iberian Peninsula.
sevilla-es.tagline: Capital of Andalusia and the Province of Seville, Spain.
activities: Climb the bell tower or castle for the rooftops view
Catch sunset from a riverside or hillside vantage point
Browse the weekly market for produce and crafts
Walk a circuit of the centro storico and main square
tips: Lunch menus are often half the price of evening menus for the same dish.
Most museums shut one weekday — usually Monday or Tuesday.

valencia-es.name: Valencia
valencia-es.general: Valencia, known officially in Valencian as València, is the capital and largest city of the Valencian Community and the province of the same name in Spain. It is located on the banks of the Turia, on the east coast of the Iberian Peninsula on the Mediterranean Sea. With a population of 824,340, it is the third most-populous city in Spain.
activities: Take a half-day boat tour to a nearby cove

Walk a coastal path out of town for the panoramic view back
Stroll the seafront and old harbour at dusk
tips: Many beaches charge for loungers; public stretches are free if you bring a towel.
The first ferry of the morning is the quietest if you're island-hopping.

valladolid-es.tagline: Municipality in Castile and León, Spain.
activities: Browse the weekly market for produce and crafts

Catch sunset from a riverside or hillside vantage point

tips: Regional train tickets sometimes need stamping or scanning before boarding.

zaragoza-es.name: Zaragoza
zaragoza-es.general: Zaragoza, traditionally known in English as Saragossa, is the capital city of the province of Zaragoza and of the autonomous community of Aragon, Spain. It lies by the Ebro river and its tributaries, the Huerva and the Gállego, roughly in the centre of both Aragon and the Ebro basin.
activities: Walk a circuit of the centro storico and main square
Climb the bell tower or castle for the rooftops view
Browse the weekly market for produce and crafts
Visit the cathedral and the city's flagship museum
tips: Most museums shut one weekday — usually Monday or Tuesday.
Lunch menus are often half the price of evening menus for the same dish.
Dinner starts late — restaurants open after 20:00

gothenburg-se.name: Gothenburg
gothenburg-se.general: Gothenburg is the second-largest city in Sweden, after the capital Stockholm, and the fifth-largest in the Nordic countries. Situated by the Kattegat on the west coast of Sweden 400 km from the capital, it is the gubernatorial seat of Västra Götaland County, with a population of approximately 600,000 in the city proper and about 1.1 million inhabitants in the metropolitan area.
activities: Climb to the citadel or ramparts above the bay
Take a half-day boat tour to a nearby cove
Sample the regional seafood at a quayside taverna
Walk a coastal path out of town for the panoramic view back
tips: Cruise-port days flood the old town for a few hours — check the cruise schedule.
Many beaches charge for loungers; public stretches are free if you bring a towel.
Card-only is common — little cash needed

malmo-se.name: Malmö
malmo-se.general: Malmö is the third-largest city in Sweden, after Stockholm and Gothenburg, and the seventh-largest city in the Nordic region. Located on the Öresund strait on the southwestern coast of Sweden, it is the largest city in Scania, with a municipal population of 365,644 in 2024, and is the gubernatorial seat of Skåne County.

Walk a coastal path out of town for the panoramic view back
Take a half-day boat tour to a nearby cove
tips: Many beaches charge for loungers; public stretches are free if you bring a towel.
The first ferry of the morning is the quietest if you're island-hopping.
Alcohol sold at Systembolaget — plan ahead

stockholm-se.name: Stockholm
stockholm-se.general: Stockholm is the capital and most populous city of Sweden, as well as the largest urban area in the Nordic countries. Approximately 1 million people live in the municipality, with 1.6 million in the urban area, and 2.5 million in the metropolitan area. The city stretches across fourteen islands where Lake Mälaren flows into the Baltic Sea.
stockholm-se.tagline: Capital and most populous city of Sweden.
activities: Ride a tram or vaporetto across the historic centre
Walk the historic waterfront at golden hour
Climb the city's highest viewpoint for a panoramic sweep
Try the city's signature seafood dish at a local konoba/taverna
tips: Ferries to popular islands sell out fast in summer — book ahead.
Tap water is fine in most coastal capitals — refill a bottle to save money.
Midsummer empties cities

bern-ch.general: Bern, or Berne, is the de facto capital of Switzerland, referred to as the "federal city". The Bern agglomeration, which includes 36 municipalities, had a population of 406,900 in 2014. The metropolitan area had a population of 660,000 in 2000.
bern-ch.tagline: city in Switzerland, capital of the canton of Bern and de facto capital of Switzerland.
activities: Walk the historic core's main square circuit

Pick one flagship museum and skip the second
tips: Funiculars and trams are often a faster shortcut than walking uphill.
Weather can shift fast in mountain capitals — check the forecast hour by hour.

odesa-ua.general: Odesa, also spelled Odessa, is the third-most populous city and municipality in Ukraine and a major seaport and transport hub located in the south-west of the country, on the northwestern shore of the Black Sea. The total administrative area is 864 square kilometres (334 sq mi) and includes a significant amount of rural land.
sevastopol-ua.tagline: Largest city on the Crimean peninsula.

edinburgh-gb.name: Edinburgh
edinburgh-gb.general: Edinburgh is the capital city of Scotland and one of its 32 council areas. It is located in southeast Scotland and is bounded to the north by the Firth of Forth and to the south by the Pentland Hills. Edinburgh had a population of 506,520 in 2020, making it the second-most-populous city in Scotland and the seventh-most-populous in the United Kingdom.
activities: Stroll the seafront and old harbour at dusk
Sample the regional seafood at a quayside taverna
Walk a coastal path out of town for the panoramic view back
Climb to the citadel or ramparts above the bay
tips: Coastal cities heat up after 11:00 in summer — start sights early.
The first ferry of the morning is the quietest if you're island-hopping.
Museum entry often free — donations welcome

manchester-gb.general: Manchester is a city and metropolitan borough in North West England, at the centre of the eponymous county of Greater Manchester. It had a population of over 589,000 in 2024. The two cities and the surrounding towns form one of the United Kingdom's most populous conurbations, the Greater Manchester Built-up Area, which has a population of 2.87 million.
manchester-gb.tagline: City and metropolitan borough in England.

nottingham-gb.name: Nottingham
nottingham-gb.general: Nottingham is a city and unitary authority area in Nottinghamshire, East Midlands, England. It is located 42 miles (68 km) south-east of Sheffield and 54 miles (87 km) north-east of Birmingham. Nottingham is the legendary home of Robin Hood's belligerent Sheriff of Nottingham, and is historically associated with the lace-making, bicycle and tobacco industries.
nottingham-gb.tagline: City and council area in Nottinghamshire, England.

Try the regional dish at a back-street trattoria
Catch sunset from a riverside or hillside vantage point
Browse the weekly market for produce and crafts
tips: Most museums shut one weekday — usually Monday or Tuesday.
Cash still appears at smaller bakeries and family restaurants.
Rain any day — pack a compact umbrella

vaduz-li.name: Vaduz
vaduz-li.general: Vaduz is the capital of Liechtenstein and also the seat of the national parliament. The town, which is located along the Rhine, has 5,696 residents. It is home to the reigning prince of Liechtenstein and the Liechtenstein princely family. The town's distinctive architecture is also displayed in landmarks such as the Cathedral of St.

Visit the cathedral and climb its bell tower for the rooftops

san-marino-sm.name: San Marino
san-marino-sm.general: The City of San Marino, also known simply as San Marino and locally as Città, is the capital city of the Republic of San Marino and one of its nine castelli. It has a population of 4,118. It is on the western slopes of San Marino's highest point, Monte Titano.
san-marino-sm.tagline: Capital city and Castello in San Marino.
activities: Take a ferry or harbour cruise across the bay
Walk the historic waterfront at golden hour
Visit the old port and the lighthouse at dusk
Climb the city's highest viewpoint for a panoramic sweep
tips: Old-town stone is slick after rain — pack grippy shoes.

vatican-city-va.name: Vatican City
vatican-city-va.general: Vatican City, officially the Vatican City State, often shortened as the Vatican, is a landlocked sovereign city-state in Southern Europe. Ruled by the pope, it is an enclave within the city of Rome, Italy, and serves as the administrative centre of the Catholic Church.
activities: Visit a flagship botanical garden or city park late afternoon
